name: Lingnan
notes:
Battle-test round targeting Lingnan's SGS taught-postgraduate index. The index page's ~94 raw candidates (LLM-filtered) resolve to ~47 real programmes once same-row duplicate collapse removes the stub+"Visit Website" pairs the filter selects as separate candidates. detail.md/detail.html are the Master of Science in Finance department homepage (chosen as the richest self-contained candidate: 13 requirements, full tuition/study-mode/deadline coverage), fetched directly rather than via the SGS routing-stub + supplement path.

This round's real finding was architectural, not a content-extraction bug: most Lingnan programmes publish an SGS "detail page" that is a pure routing stub (name + application period only) while the real admission content (tuition, requirements, study mode) lives one-to-two hops away on an independently-run department site, reachable only via a same-index-row "Visit Website" sibling link. Added a new generic mechanism (src/services/thin_page_supplement.py) that detects a missing-tuition extraction at runtime (any university, no registry entry) and expands via bounded sibling + admission-keyword-ranked sub-link fetches, re-extracting on the merged content. Also fixed: same-row candidate duplicate collapse (the LLM candidate filter selects both the stub and its sibling as separate top-level candidates, roughly doubling the true programme count), a same-threshold requirement dedup gap (a terse "TOEFL 79" and a full sentence stating the identical fact were extracted as two requirements, since neither substring containment nor text-similarity dedup catches a length mismatch that large), and a noise-name vocabulary gap (department-page furniture headings — hero banners, fee/scholarship section titles, HTML <title> site names — were slipping through as fake "programme names" once the supplement mechanism merged that content in).
